statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. The Nasdaq-100 closed at 28,945.06, up 0.02%, after recovering 192 points from a 28,753.29 session low, so the hawkish post-press-conference slide was substantially retraced rather than extended. VIX closed at 17.71 against an 18.94 session high. Tail sits at the watch threshold rather than lower because the 2-year yield closed at a 52-week high of 4.742%, up 7.9 basis points and at its own session high, leaving the front-end repricing unresolved.
recommendation: Tail is back below the block threshold because the specific condition that justified the previous reading, a one-way decline with no retracement, was invalidated inside the final hour of cash trade. The index recovered 192 points off its low into the close, implied volatility decayed from its session high, and crude fell 3.51% on reports that roughly half of the damaged Saudi East-West pipeline may restart within days. What remains unresolved is the front end: the 2-year closed at a 52-week high and at its session high, which keeps the mapped state at WATCH rather than returning it to the low band. The narrow danger window covers the current post-close hour only. The highest modelled risk in the forward path is the 13:30 UTC cash open on September 17, which follows the first post-hike data block by one hour; that remains a conditional checkpoint and no opening continuation is treated as observed.
headline: Nasdaq-100 recovers 192 points off its low to close flat at 28,945.06, invalidating the post-FOMC one-way path, while the 2-year yield ends at a 52-week high
body: The FOMC raised the federal funds target range by 25 basis points to 3.75-4.00% at 18:00 UTC in a unanimous 12-0 vote, stating that inflation remains elevated and that the action supports a timelier return to the 2 percent goal, with projections showing a median expectation of one further hike this year. The initial reaction was risk-positive, then reversed sharply during Chair Warsh's press conference, taking the index from 29,235.89 to a 28,753.29 low. The decisive evidence for this assessment is what happened next: the Nasdaq-100 recovered 192 points into the 20:00 UTC cash close, finishing at 28,945.06, up 0.02% on the day. The pathological no-retracement path that the previous run scored as underway did not persist. Breadth remained poor, with the Dow down 1.21% at 51,461.90 and the S&P 500 down 0.45% at 7,551.81 against a Nasdaq Composite that closed down 0.01%, so the index-level recovery was concentrated in megacap technology and semiconductors, where Intel gained on reports of SK Hynix manufacturing talks. Volatility decayed: VIX closed at 17.71 after trading as high as 18.94. Rates did not stabilise in the same way. The 2-year yield closed at 4.742%, up 7.9 basis points, at both a 52-week high and its session high, while the 5-year rose 3.3 basis points to 4.859% and the 10-year added a basis point to 5.01%, a bear-flattening consistent with a hawkish policy repricing rather than a growth scare. Crude fell sharply, with WTI down 3.51% to $102.12 and Brent down 2.97% to $105.52, after reports that Saudi Aramco aims to restore roughly half of the drone-damaged East-West pipeline within days, with full capacity targeted in about six weeks. That removes some of the acute supply premium built up during the Iran conflict and the Strait of Hormuz disruption, though the conflict itself remains an unresolved overnight headline channel and has already caused direct technology-sector damage through strikes affecting cloud infrastructure in the region. The combination of an observed retracement, decaying implied volatility and an easing oil premium supports a materially lower Tail than the previous hour, while the unretraced front-end move and poor breadth keep Stress high and hold the mapped state at the watch threshold for the current post-close hour.

lookbackSummary: Across the past 24 hours the published Claude state ran 20 at Tuesday's U.S. close, eased into the low band overnight and bottomed at 13 at 01:00 UTC as the Asian and European sessions held a contained normal range, running 14-16 through the European morning. It returned to the watch band at 12:00 UTC with the U.S. pre-market, held 20-22 through the afternoon, and rose to 24 at 18:00 UTC as the FOMC statement landed. The single highest reading of the window was 31 at 19:00 UTC, published while the index sat at its session low during the Warsh press conference with no retracement yet formed. That reading captured the observed structure at the time; the recovery into the cash close has since invalidated its continuation premise, which is why the current reading is eleven points lower.
outlookSummary: The forecast opens at 20 for the current post-close hour, returns to the low band from 21:00 UTC and runs a 16-17 overnight floor, above a typical quiet night because live Middle East supply headlines remain an open channel rather than because of any observed index structure. It drifts to 18 into the European morning, then rises to 21 for the 12:00 UTC hour containing jobless claims, the Philadelphia Fed index, housing starts and building permits, and peaks at 23 for the 13:30 UTC cash open, the highest modelled value in the window because a post-policy-shift opening auction is where one-way structure would establish if it is going to. That peak is explicitly conditional. The path then decays through 22, 21 and 20 across the U.S. morning and returns to 19 from 17:00 UTC on September 17. Stress stays in the high band throughout, easing from 75 to a 63-65 overnight trough before rebounding to 76 at the open, reflecting an environment that remains difficult without implying a lethal price path.
